reviews.title: Fails at its one job
reviews.text:
Even for the most basic usage of this app, the ui is invasive and irritating. I had to delete it because of the recent update, which puts this irritating little character on my lock screen, just begging me to ‘check in’ and ‘see what drains your energy’. I checked my notification settings for Flo and they’re completely off, so I don’t know how they managed to do this, but it was completely unwelcome and I couldn’t figure out how to turn it off.

I’ve long thought that Flo is overcomplicated. Some people want to track their cycle more closely than me, and maybe appreciate the push to get in touch with their mood and health, but when the app specifically asks you what you want to use the app for, and then pushes a bunch of other stuff you didn’t ask for, it feels completely futile. They have these discussion forums which might be helpful for some, but for me act as a total time suck, same as most social media. The questions are so obviously divisive and personal that they function really well as ragebait or to invite traumadumping, but they have the excuse of the app being intimate in nature so they can ask such personal questions. They also have the pretense of being helpful with all these blog posts about pleasure and health, but they’re all locked behind a paywall. To an extent I understand, because it’s a for profit app, but when it’s framed as “is this bad for you?” Or “is this normal?” It comes across as scummy, clickbaity fearmongering.

reviews.title: Non Inclusive, Money Hungry, AI Robots
reviews.text: Flo used to be my best friend when starting my period journey. I downloaded it after my first period in 8th grade and used it religiously over several years. The last few years as I slowly but surely used it less and less. I had become very good at predicting my period based on PMS symptoms and the fact i’ve always had a very on schedule and predictable cycle. When I started dating my girlfriend, Flo introduced the new “partner” feature which Initially made me think I had a new reason to use the app. But I very quickly realized that this is a purely heterosexual, male and female feature. I have not opened the app since. Until today, to check and see if they had updated it after several years. It’s been over two years since this new feature and they have yet to make it more inclusive. They even say it’s only for male and female relationships. Their only excuse is being unable to track two cycles but working everyday to be more inclusive blah blah. I don’t see how tracking two cycles is an issue when each partner has their own account. each account tracks the cycle of the user attached to it. the only thing the partner portion does it let the other partner see their cycle. it is honestly so obvious that they aren’t investing the time into making it more inclusive because it’s definitely not that hard to do seeing as how they’re half way there already.

reviews.title: Manipulative & misleading
reviews.text:
Boy my respect for this company has gone down the toilet.

The app has invasive pop-ups for premium every day that I open the app. Irritating compared to less invasive advertising methods like a banner at the top/bottom of the app, but whatever. 

However, I got an ad pop-up today for a VIP sale that I couldn’t close at all without closing the app. There was literally no button to close it. You’re putting blocks between women accessing their personal data on their cycle to coerce them into giving you money. Extremely icky. 

There’s also the matter of the ‘cycle trends’ graph. As a non-premium user, I was extremely alarmed when this graph read ‘abnormal’ in two places and spent some time going through my past few cycles on my calendar to see what the issue was. Finding none, I went back to the graph and only then came to the conclusion that this wasn’t MY graph — it was *a* graph. There’s nothing that states that the graph was an example — just that ‘Unlock Premium’ button. Extremely manipulative and misleading. 

For an app about women’s health and wellbeing, this is an absolute joke. Blocking access to your users’ own health data and intentionally misrepresenting potential health issues to coerce them into buying premium is ethically questionable and extremely disrespectful.

Ah, not to mention the VERY excessive personal data collected about you, ranging from your health and fitness to your search history and more. Honestly, don’t use this app. There are better alternative

I’ve used the app in the past when I was trying to get pregnant.  It seemed like it had some good tools to help you on that journey.  We ultimately ended up not being able to continue trying, and I updated the app to reflect that we were not trying to get pregnant, I just wanted to track my period.  The app however continued to send me near constant tips on how to get pregnant and reminders of when I was in the ideal conception window for months!  It was just a terrible, sad gut punch every time and I ended up having to delete the app.

Today I saw a post about their new perimenopause/menopause tool, including a quiz to score where you are on the journey.
The questions include a whole section on when your last period was so they can calculate whether you are officially in menopause.  Helpful except theres literally no way to tell it if the lack of periods are a medical issue, like the hysterectomy I had a little over a year ago, so it can’t give me even remotely accurate info.  But the worst part is to access this tool, you are required to give them permission for them and their third party partners to have unfettered access to and the ability to share all information you provide, including personal info.  There is no option to opt out at all.  It’s shady to be sure, and I think shows what the company really values (your data not your health).

reviews.title: Don’t recommend for conception or pregnancy planning
reviews.text:
I really regret paying for this app. I found that it increased my anxiety and sadness rather than being supportive, and I’ve since deleted it (even though I am still paying for it 😞)

The app has an intense focus on pregnancy with very little practical guidance around conception itself. For example, the day after ovulation it begins discussing early pregnancy symptoms and what pregnancy looks like at “1 day,” despite this being scientifically implausible — pregnancy symptoms cannot occur that early. This constant emphasis on pregnancy felt misleading and heightened my anxiety rather than helping me feel informed or supported. I’ve since switched to another app that focuses more appropriately on hormone regulation and relaxation during the luteal phase, which feels far healthier.

I also found Flo to be very glitchy and rigid in how it handles user data. It pulls information from your phone but offers little ability to properly contextualise or correct it. For instance, I didn’t have a period for years due to having a Mirena, yet the app repeatedly flags me as having a history of abnormal cycles. Despite multiple attempts to edit this, it continually prompts me to complete surveys about abnormal periods, which feels inaccurate and frustrating.

Overall, I found the app anxiety-inducing, inflexible, and poorly aligned with evidence-based fertility tracking.
